classification.difficultyReason: Requires deriving two linear branches from an absolute-value denominator and preserving the excluded input through cancellation. The rating is independent of the source pictogram.

inlines.text: Factor the numerator, then use the two sign cases for

answer.worked:
The original denominator is zero at $x=1$, so $x\ne1$.

The difference-of-squares factorisation follows by expansion:
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)(x+1)&=x^2+x-x-1\\(x-1)(x+1)&=x^2-1.\end{align*}$$

For $x<1$, $|x-1|=-(x-1)$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{-(x-1)}\\y&=-(x+1)\\y&=-x-1.\end{align*}$$

For $x>1$, $|x-1|=x-1$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-1}\\y&=x+1.\end{align*}$$

The left branch passes through $(-1,0)$ and $(0,-1)$ and has an open endpoint at $(1,-2)$. The right branch has an open endpoint at $(1,2)$ and gradient $1$. Both endpoints are open because $x=1$ remains excluded after cancellation.
